security_audit.summary: All 21 static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or ordinary Java identifiers; the skill executes no external commands. remediation.issue: Logging and validation examples can expose email addresses, rejected values, or exception details.
remediation.suggestion: Use allowlisted fields, mask personal data, omit rejected values, and sanitize validation messages before logging or returning them.

content.value_statement: Inconsistent exceptions and responses make Spring services difficult to maintain. This skill provides reusable patterns for handlers, error codes, responses, validation, and logging.
actual_capabilities: Defines a BusinessException hierarchy linked to centralized error codes.
Shows domain exceptions for missing entities, duplicate resources, authentication, and authorization.
Provides a Spring RestControllerAdvice pattern for business, validation, and unexpected exceptions.
Defines a consistent error response with codes, messages, field errors, and timestamps.
Demonstrates service-layer exception use and recommended application logging levels.
limitations: Examples require adaptation to each project's packages, dependencies, error codes, and language.
The skill does not generate runnable files or execute tests.
It does not cover reactive Spring, distributed tracing, or framework-specific security handlers.
Examples need additional redaction controls before processing sensitive fields.

use_cases.title: Create a Spring API Error Standard
use_cases.description: Design shared exception classes, error codes, and response fields for a new Spring service.

use_cases.title: Align Existing Service Errors
use_cases.description: Review inconsistent exception paths and map them to one global handling approach.

use_cases.title: Define Backend Review Criteria
use_cases.description: Build checks for status codes, exception types, response consistency, and appropriate logging.

prompt_templates.title: Create One Domain Exception
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Spring business exception for [condition] using HTTP status [status] and error code [code]. Explain the mapping.
prompt_templates.scenario: Begin with one clear exception requirement.

prompt_templates.title: Design an Error Response
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a consistent error response for [service]. Include business errors, validation details, and timestamps while excluding sensitive values.
prompt_templates.scenario: Define a response contract for a Spring REST API.

prompt_templates.title: Implement a Global Handler
prompt_templates.prompt: Implement a global Spring exception handler for these exceptions: [list]. Map status codes and specify sanitized logging behavior.
prompt_templates.scenario: Connect several exception types to centralized handling.

prompt_templates.title: Audit an Error Handling Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Spring error handling design: [design]. Identify inconsistent mappings, exposure risks, missing cases, and migration steps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Evaluate an established service and plan improvements.

output_examples.input: Design handling for a missing customer record.
output_examples.output: Use a customer-specific business exception mapped to the shared not-found code and HTTP 404. Return a stable message without internal details.

output_examples.input: Review validation failure handling for account registration.
output: Map invalid fields to the shared validation error code and HTTP 400.
Return field names and safe messages.
Do not return passwords, tokens, or raw rejected values.

output_examples.input: Choose logging levels for common failures.
output_examples.output: Log expected business failures at warning level and unexpected system failures at error level. Mask personal data and include stable error codes.

best_practices: Keep error codes stable and map each code to one intended HTTP status.
Centralize response creation and exception mapping in a global handler.
Redact sensitive values from logs, exception messages, and validation responses.
anti_patterns: Do not return stack traces or internal exception details to API clients.
Do not log passwords, tokens, raw credentials, or unrestricted request values.
Do not create unrelated response shapes for each controller.

faq.question: Which Spring applications fit this skill?
faq.answer: It targets Java Spring REST services using controller advice, service layers, and structured error responses.

faq.question: Does it provide complete production code?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns that require project-specific imports, packages, policies, and tests.

faq.question: Can I change the error code format?
faq.answer: Yes. Keep the chosen format stable, documented, and unique across the service.

faq.question: How should validation errors be returned?
faq.answer: Return safe field names and messages under one validation code. Omit raw values when they may contain sensitive data.

faq.question: How should unexpected exceptions be logged?
faq.answer: Log them at error level with a stable correlation identifier. Return a generic client message.

faq.question: Does this skill execute commands or modify files?
faq.answer: No. The source is guidance with Java and response examples; it contains no executable scripts.
